policy_presence.summary: The University of Melbourne distributes AI policy across Subject Coordinator instructions, the Student Academic Integrity Policy (MPF1310), the Responsible Conduct of Research Policy (MPF1318 cl 5.11), and the University AI Principles.

ai_disclosure.summary: University of Melbourne guidance mandates a dual disclosure framework: citing AI outputs in the reference list when quoting or paraphrasing does not replace an acknowledgement declaration; students must provide both a citation and a process declaration describing how tools were used, with unauthorised or undisclosed use constituting misconduct under MPF1310.

coursework.summary: At the University of Melbourne, each Subject Coordinator sets the boundaries of appropriate GenAI use in their subject; students must check before using AI for assessment-related work and produce the submitted work themselves unless explicitly authorized.

exams.summary: In University of Melbourne examinations, students must verify whether GenAI is authorised by the Subject Coordinator or exam instructions, and if permitted, use only approved tools and specified permitted uses. Tool access conveys no exam authorization, and unauthorised or undisclosed AI use in exams constitutes academic misconduct under MPF1310.

privacy_data_entry.summary: Students and researchers must not upload personal data, private information, third-party copyright, or patentable IP to external AI platforms. University teaching and assessment IP must remain within SparkAI or sanctioned environments; student LMS interactions and AILA session metadata are retained and reviewable by authorized decision-makers under the LMS privacy collection notice.

academic_integrity.summary: Under MPF1310, unauthorised or undisclosed technology use in assessable work constitutes academic misconduct. Poor Academic Practice is managed educatively by Subject Coordinators, distinct from formal Faculty Level 1 and Serious Level 2 misconduct. Turnitin AI detection reports serve as an investigative prompt rather than proof, students have the right to provide drafts and explanations in exploratory discussions, and MPF1323 establishes a 20-university-business-day appeal window.

approved_tools.summary: The University of Melbourne provides AILA within Canvas LMS where enabled by coordinators, SparkAI as a secure internal platform for staff (student access prohibited), Turnitin AI writing detection as an investigative diagnostic in similarity reports, and M365 Copilot Chat for student study support. Institutional access conveys neither coursework nor examination permission.

named_ai_services.summary: The University of Melbourne provides AILA within Canvas LMS where enabled by coordinators, SparkAI as a secure internal platform for staff (student access prohibited), Turnitin AI writing detection as an investigative diagnostic in similarity reports, and M365 Copilot Chat for student study support. Institutional access conveys neither coursework nor examination permission.

teaching_guidance.summary: Melbourne teaching guidance advises Subject Coordinators to establish clear subject AI boundaries, model transparency, and provide guidance on translation and editing tool limits. GenAI tools must never substitute for staff evaluative judgement in marking or grading. Subjects are designed with at least 50% secure assessments to assure learning, supported by CSHE pedagogical assessment enhancement strategies.

research_guidance.summary: Under section 5.11 of the Responsible Conduct of Research Policy (MPF1318) and active University guidance, researchers must document DAT use, disclose tools in outputs, and obtain privacy/security/ethics approvals. For graduate research theses, AI editing is strictly restricted to minor language and clarity support under Australian Standards for Editing Practice, with supervisor AI review requiring explicit written candidate consent.

security_procurement.summary: The University of Melbourne AI Principles establish an overarching governance framework emphasizing fairness, literacy, privacy, and security; staff testing of assessment materials must remain within SparkAI or sanctioned environments rather than public third-party services.
